# Willow House: demo content pack

**Version 2.** Willow House is one house in the fictional Lantern Row Housing Co-op. The site now has a co-op common room, a second house and a repairs team drawn from both houses. Shared library pages add examples of finding an answer across groups. Willow's original people, records and figures stay with Willow; garden activity stays in its stream and events.

Content for the live demo site behind the landing page. Everything here is fictional. Dates inside library documents are fixed (12 March). Everything in the stream, events, poll, decisions, fund and messages is given as days relative to install day (day 0). "Day -2" means two days before install; "day +5" means five days after.

Notes for whoever loads this:

- The story in one paragraph: in March the back steps had two loose treads and the house agreed to get three quotes. Ana got them in April (Hollis the joiner was cheapest at 600 PRACTICE in the practice example). The house waited for its practice fund to be created and for the house decision, then paid Hollis, leaving 400 PRACTICE above its 200 PRACTICE floor. He asks to be paid when booked because he buys the hardwood first; he has not come yet. Two days before install Rosa posts that a third board is now loose too; Jo offers to get three quotes for that, because the house rules say any repair over 300 PRACTICE needs three quotes.
- The landing-page answer cites House minutes, 12 March. The Repair log also mentions the back steps (it has to). After loading, ask "Has anyone looked at the back steps?" and check that the citation is the minutes. If retrieval picks the Repair log instead, the minutes passage is the one to favour.
- The fund uses Practice Money (PRACTICE), with no real value. It receives 1,000 PRACTICE once at creation and no later outside income. Say so wherever it is shown. All people, organisations, tradespeople and costs in this pack are made up. None describes a real co-op, supplier, city or law.
- There are four flat groups, with no parent or child groups. The co-op is the site, not a group containing the houses. The 19 seeded people each belong to the Co-op common room and their own house. Some also belong to Co-op Repairs.
- Audience labels apply to each library page: **public** means anyone, including signed-out visitors; **community** means any signed-in person, even before joining the page's group; **members-only** means members of that page's group. Public About text does not open private records. Publish only the page bodies and About text as content; loader instructions and expected answers are not library pages.
(note removed)
- Seeded counts are a starting snapshot. A visitor joining the demo later adds a member; that does not rewrite the opening rosters or responses of Willow's existing decisions.

Find shared tools, people we have hired, joining notes and co-op meeting notes. You can join this group on the demo. Anyone can read the shared-tools page; sign in to read the other shared pages. Anyone may join Willow House on this demo to explore its made-up records. A real house is invitation-only. Joining the demo does not give you a room or create a tenancy. The fund uses practice money.

**Rowan House**

> We are seven people living in the other house at Lantern Row Housing Co-op. Our house records are for our members. Membership is by invitation. We have shared one page with the whole co-op: Replacing our boiler: notes for another house. Sign in to read it; you do not need to join Rowan.

**Co-op Repairs**

> We are six people from Willow House and Rowan House who help arrange repairs and look after shared tools. Ask Ana about a Willow job, Ben about a Rowan job, and Jo or Ari about borrowing tools. Membership is by invitation. Each house keeps its own records and makes its own spending decisions.

### Bylaws

Group: Willow House. Audience: **members-only**.

**Bylaws of Willow House, Lantern Row Housing Co-op**

1. Name and purpose. Willow House is one house in Lantern Row Housing Co-op. These bylaws apply to Willow House. The members run the house together and live in it. The house has 12 rooms and up to 12 members. Rowan House has its own house records.

2. Members. A member is someone who lives in the house, has paid the $500 member share, and has been agreed by a house decision. The share is paid back within 60 days of leaving, less anything owed. Each member has one voice in decisions.

3. House charge. Each member pays a monthly house charge, set in the yearly budget. It is due by the 5th of the month. If you are going to be late, tell the treasurer before the 5th, not after.

4. Officers. Each January the house picks a treasurer, a minutes-taker, a keeper of the repair log and three fund approvers. One person can do more than one job. Any of these can be changed by a house decision at any time.

5. House decisions. Most decisions are made on the house site. Any member can propose one. A proposal says what will happen, what it costs if anything, and when it closes.

Each member responds in one of three ways:

- Agree.
- Stand aside. You won't stop it, but you have doubts or don't want to take part. A reason is welcome but not needed.
- Block. You think this would harm the house and should not go ahead. You cannot Block without writing a reason.

A decision passes when, by the deadline, at least two-thirds of the house has responded (8 of 12 when the house is full), at least one member has agreed, and nobody has blocked.

Deadlines: 7 days for everyday decisions and money decisions. 14 days for changing these bylaws or the house rules.

If a decision does not pass, the person who proposed it can change it and bring it back as a new decision. If someone blocks, talk to them first. Most blocks point at something that can be fixed.

6. The repair fund. The demo fund receives 1,000 PRACTICE once at creation; house charges and spare household money never top it up. Any payment from the fund needs approval from two of the three fund approvers. A payment over 300 PRACTICE also needs a house decision first. The fund should not go below 200 PRACTICE except in an emergency, meaning roof, heating, water, or anything unsafe.

7. Meetings. The house meets once a month. Minutes go in the library. Small things can be agreed at a meeting if two-thirds of the house is there and nobody blocks. Anything else goes on the site.

8. Leaving. Give one month's notice to the treasurer and the house.

9. Changing these bylaws. By house decision, open for 14 days.

### House rules

Group: Willow House. Audience: **members-only**.

These are the rules we have agreed. They change by house decision, open for 14 days. The guest rule was last changed that way.

**Quiet hours.** 10 pm to 7 am, every night. Keep music and calls in your room, doors closed. Owen sleeps late after shifts, so go easy on the stairs in the mornings.

**Kitchen and fridge.** Wash up the same day. Each person has a labelled fridge shelf; don't move someone else's food to make room. The shelf in the door is shared (milk, butter, sauces). Anything unlabelled on the bottom shelf after a week goes on the side with a note, then out.

**Guests.** A guest can stay up to 7 nights in a row. Post in the stream if a guest is staying more than one night. Longer stays need a house decision. Guests follow quiet hours and wash their own dishes.

**Bikes.** Bikes go in the bike shed, not the hall. The hall has to stay clear.

**Shared rooms.** The front room is for everyone. If you book it for something, post in the stream at least two days ahead.

**Smoking.** Not inside. Outside, away from the windows, and take your ends with you.

**Pets.** No new pets without a house decision.

**Repairs.** Report anything broken to Ana or add it to the Repair log. Under $300, Willow's members of Co-op Repairs can just get it done. Over $300 needs three quotes and a house decision. Payments from the repair fund need two of the three fund approvers.

**How we decide.** House decisions are made by consensus on the site. Each member responds Agree, Stand aside, or Block. A Block needs a written reason. A decision passes when at least two-thirds of the house has responded by the deadline, someone agrees and nobody blocks. Everyday and money decisions are open for 7 days. Changing these rules or the bylaws is open for 14 days.

**Bins.** Bins out on Tuesday night. See the chore rota for whose turn it is.

**Be decent.** If something bothers you, talk to the person first. If that doesn't work, bring it to the monthly meeting.

### Budget

Group: Willow House. Audience: **members-only**.

**Willow House budget for the year.** Agreed at the house meeting on 12 January. Jo keeps the books.

**Money in**

12 members pay a house charge of $725 a month.

| | Monthly | Yearly |
|---|---|---|
| House charges (12 x $725) | $8,700 | $104,400 |

**Money out**

| | Monthly | Yearly |
|---|---|---|
| Mortgage | $5,400 | $64,800 |
| Property tax and insurance | $1,050 | $1900 |
| Gas, electric and water | $1,150 | $13,800 |
| Internet | $90 | $1,080 |
| Household supplies (cleaning, loo roll, bulbs) | $230 | $2,760 |
| Garden | $80 | $960 |
| Household repair allowance, outside the practice fund | $700 | $8,400 |
| **Total** | **$8,700** | **$104,400** |

Money in and money out match. Nothing is left over on purpose: spare household money stays in the fictional household budget and is not a practice-fund deposit.

**Notes**

Gas and electric are higher in winter and lower in summer. The $1,150 is an average. Jo moves money between months, so don't panic at the January bill.

Household supplies: Liam buys the big packs once a month. Keep receipts and give them to Jo.

Garden: $80 a month covers seeds, compost and small tools. Grace keeps the receipts.

**The repair fund**

The practice fund receives 1,000 PRACTICE once at creation and no other outside income. Keep at least 200 PRACTICE for emergencies (roof, heating, water, anything unsafe), as the Bylaws say. The separate $700 monthly household repair allowance and older repair-log costs are fictional household-budget records, not extra practice-fund transfers.

The practice fund began at 1,000 PRACTICE. The back steps (Hollis the joiner, 600 PRACTICE) leave 400 PRACTICE, above the 200 PRACTICE floor. The job waited for creation and the house decision, not for monthly contributions.

Expected practice-fund costs; only the back steps have been paid:

- Back steps, $600 (agreed by house decision)
- Gutter over the kitchen window, about $40
- Boiler service, $18
- Small fixes as they come, usually under $100 each

After the back steps, the quoted gutter work (40 PRACTICE) and boiler service (18 PRACTICE), if later agreed and paid, would leave 342 PRACTICE. Paying the separate pending tap (140 PRACTICE) as well would leave 202 PRACTICE, still above the 200 floor. No future contribution is assumed; Jo will report at each meeting.

### Handbook

Group: Willow House. Audience: **members-only**.

**Welcome to Willow House.** Farah keeps this handbook. If something here is out of date, tell her.

**Moving in**

Farah will meet you on moving day with your keys: front door, back door, your room, and the bike shed. If you lose a key, tell Farah. She holds the spares. Before you move in you pay the $500 member share (you get it back when you leave) and your first month's house charge of $725 to Jo.

Your room should be clean and empty when you arrive. If anything is broken, tell Ana and it goes in the Repair log, so nobody blames you later.

You get a labelled shelf in the fridge and a cupboard in the kitchen. Ask Farah which ones are free. The top left fridge shelf is Pete's. It has been Pete's for years.

**Chores**

Liam runs the chore rota. It's on the fridge and changes every Monday. Jobs are: kitchen, bathrooms, hall and stairs, bins, front room. New members start on the rota in their second week.

Bins go out on Tuesday night. Recycling (blue lid) goes out every other week. The rota says which week. If you can't do your turn, swap with someone and tell Liam.

**Guests**

Guests are welcome. A guest can stay up to 7 nights in a row. If someone is staying more than one night, post it in the stream. Longer stays need a house decision.

**Quiet hours**

10 pm to 7 am, every night. Owen works late shifts and sleeps in, so please go easy on the stairs in the mornings.

**Meetings and decisions**

The house meets once a month in the front room. Sam chairs, Mei takes minutes. Bigger things are decided on the house site: you'll get a notice, and you respond Agree, Stand aside, or Block. If you Block, you write why.

**Who to ask**

| For | Ask |
|---|---|
| Keys, moving in, your room | Farah |
| Something broken | Ana, or add it to the Repair log |
| House charge, receipts, the fund | Jo |
| Chore rota and swaps | Liam |
| The garden | Grace |
| Bikes and the bike shed | Pete |
| Meetings, the house site | Sam |
| Old minutes | Mei |

If you're not sure, ask Rosa. She has lived here longest and usually knows.

### Shared tools: borrowing and returns

Group: Co-op common room. Audience: **public**.

Our shared cordless drill, socket set and pipe wrench live in the courtyard tool cupboard. Co-op members can borrow them for up to 48 hours (two days). Put your name, the item and its return time on the sheet inside the cupboard. Return everything clean, with all its parts, and cross your name off.

Ask Jo or Ari to arrange access. Tell them about a broken or missing part before the next person borrows it. This page is public so a visitor can see how our tool library works; borrowing is for co-op members.

### Joining a house: our first week

Group: Co-op common room. Audience: **community**.

Ask Farah at Willow House or Omar at Rowan House about a room. Each house decides who joins and explains its own house charge and member share before anyone agrees to move in. Read that house's handbook and ask about anything unclear.

The house welcome contact arranges keys, shows you shared rooms and helps you find your house group on this site. Read the chore rota together. Both houses use this common room for shared notices and knowledge; the houses keep their private records in their own groups.

On this demo, Willow lets visitors join its group to try the records. A real house is invitation-only, as Willow's About text explains. Joining a demo group is not an offer of housing.

### Replacing our boiler: notes for another house

Group: Rowan House. Audience: **community**. Author: Leah Tan.

Ellis the heating fitter replaced Rowan's boiler. The total was $4,200, including the boiler, fitting and removal of the old unit. The work took one full day.

We would ask for the included work to be written down before booking. In particular, check whether the price includes removing the old unit and clearing up. Agree the access time and choose someone to be home while the work is done.

We shared this page so another house can learn from the job. It contains no other Rowan house business.

## 8. Decisions

All four existing decision records (1, 2, 3a, 3b) belong to Willow House and are members-only. Their opening rosters stay as recorded; Rowan members are not added.

### Decision 1: Back steps, hire Hollis the joiner

- Type: money decision, open 7 days
- Opened: day -13 by Ana Kowalski
- Deadline: day -6
- Roster: 12

**Proposal:**

> Hire Hollis the joiner to fix the back steps for $600, paid from the repair fund. That covers two new hardwood treads, refixing the stringer and checking the rest. We got three quotes, as agreed at the March meeting: Hollis the joiner $600, a decking firm $800, a second carpenter $900. Hollis is the cheapest and the only one who includes taking the old treads away. He asks to be paid when he is booked, because he buys the hardwood first. The fund is now $1,000, so this leaves $400, above our $200 floor.

**Responses:**

| Member | Response | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Ana Kowalski | Agree | |
| Jo Sutherland | Agree | Fund checked, fine. |
| Rosa Martins | Agree | Please, before the frost. |
| Sam Okafor | Agree | |
| Mei Chen | Agree | |
| Marcus Bell | Agree | His quote is fair for hardwood. |
| Grace Adeyemi | Agree | |
| Farah Haddad | Agree | |
| Pete Lindqvist | Agree | |
| Liam O'Brien | Stand aside | I'd rather Marcus and I tried it first, but I won't hold it up. |
| Owen Price | Stand aside | Haven't had time to read the quotes properly. Happy to go with the house. |
| Ines Duarte | No response | (She was moving in that week.) |

Totals: 11 of 12 responded. 9 Agree, 2 Stand aside, 0 Block.

**Result: Agreed.** Two-thirds needed (8 of 12); 11 responded; 9 agreed; nobody blocked. The fund payment of $600 followed on day -5 (see The fund).

Open evening description: "Come and see how a housing co-op works. Tea in the common room, a walk round the courtyard and time for questions. No need to book."

Courtyard planting morning description: "We're planting bulbs and two new apple trees in the courtyard beds. Gloves and tools are in the tool cupboard. Anyone is welcome, children too."

Repair café description: "Bring something broken: a lamp, a chair, a bike with a flat tyre. Members who like fixing things will help you mend it and show you how. Free, with tea."

Autumn bulk-buy pickup description: "The order arrives at 9 am. We need people to carry sacks from the van to the courtyard and split them between the two houses."
